definitions_and_conventions: Expectation E is the Lebesgue integral over the underlying probability space (PDF page 1; printed page 5; Section 1.1, footnote 1).
1_E is the 0-1 indicator of event E, so 1_{t<X} indicates the strict event {t<X} (PDF page 3; printed page 7; footnote 4 and final displayed chain).
The t-integral has limits 0 and ∞, so its threshold domain is the nonnegative half-line rather than all real thresholds (PDF page 3; printed page 7; both proof displays).

The book suppresses brackets in expectation notation, so its E 1_{t<X} means the expectation of the indicator (PDF page 1; printed page 5; footnote 2, together with PDF page 3; printed page 7; final display).
implicit_context: For each threshold t, the event notation {t<X} abbreviates {ω∈Ω : t<X(ω)}; this is the structural reading of the source's random-variable and indicator notation (PDF page 1; printed page 5; probability-space convention, and PDF page 3; printed page 7; footnote 4).

The interchange is valid in the nonnegative/extended-valued setting: the integrand is an indicator and the source expressly permits infinite values (PDF page 3; printed page 7; Lemma hypothesis, finiteness sentence, and final display).

The selected claim is only the middle interchange equality, not the preceding identity EX = E∫_0^∞1_{t<X}dt or the following identification E1_{t<X}=P(t<X) (PDF page 3; printed page 7; structure of the final displayed chain and the phrase 'second equality').

Thresholds range from 0 to ∞ (PDF page 3; printed page 7; integration limits in the proof).

contract_plain_english: On the probability space underlying the chapter, let X be a non-negative random variable. For thresholds t integrated over the nonnegative half-line, the expectation of the integral of the indicator that t<X equals the integral of the expectations of those indicators: E[∫_0^∞1_{t<X}dt]=∫_0^∞E[1_{t<X}]dt. This is exactly the second equality in the proof's final chain, and the source justifies it by Fubini-Tonelli. No finite-expectation assumption is present, so the equality must retain the nonnegative extended-valued case (PDF page 1, printed page 5, expectation convention; PDF page 3, printed page 7, Lemma 1.2.1 and its proof).
